acceptance_criteria: A certificate from an issuer other than Palo Alto Networks, chaining to a trusted root, is accepted, proven by a test
A certificate that does not chain to any trusted root is rejected, proven by a test
An expired certificate is rejected, proven by a test
The pinned-fingerprint path still short-circuits verification exactly as before, proven by a test
The rejection outcome carries a fingerprint and carries no distinguished name, proven by a test asserting the absence
The report states, as measured rather than assumed, whether the runtime JVM trust store contains the corporate CA material
Backend tests and the repository privacy gate are green

baseline.authority: AGENTS.md, Palo Alto section: direct firewall evidence requires identity verification wherever the product contract defines an identity gate, and production TLS requires trusted corporate CA verification. The rule names the corporate CA as the trust root. It does not name the certificate's issuer organisation as an identity gate, and no FROZEN contract does.
baseline.engineering: main is at b360ef9. ui2/Containerfile installs corporate CA material into the OS trust store at /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and runs update-ca-trust, in both the build and the runtime stage. Whether the JVM's default trust manager reads that store depends on the base image and must be determined, not assumed. The failure message currently embeds the certificate's subject distinguished name, which is then stored in the discovery failure summary; that is tracked separately as discovery_failure_summary_stores_certificate_subject and is in scope here because this movement owns that message.
baseline.observed: Adding a Palo Alto device fails with 'Discovery did not complete'. PanXmlApiTransport's trust manager refuses any certificate whose issuer or subject distinguished name does not contain the literal 'O=Palo Alto Networks'. An enterprise firewall presents a certificate issued by the corporate CA, so that string is absent and every connection is refused before any request is sent. The check is a string match on a distinguished name, not a trust decision: it does not verify a chain, does not consult any trust store, and would accept a self-signed certificate that merely carried the right organisation name. The Product Owner's direction, recorded 2026-09-20: do not invent this control, verify against the corporate CA if it is present, and otherwise surface the situation rather than refusing on the product's own initiative.

context_not_loaded: The backup, failover and compliance planes
invariants: Trust is a verified chain, never a string match on a name
Collection failure is not a known-bad state: a certificate that cannot be verified is reported as unverifiable, not as a compromised device
Sensitive identity values are compared locally and reported as a relationship; a distinguished name is an identity value and does not belong in a stored summary
The product does not decide on the operator's behalf that a reachable device must not be reached
report.merge_gate: Open a pull request against main when the validation plan is green, and report its number in the SESSION_CLOSE. Do not merge.
report.objective: Let a Palo Alto device behind a corporate certificate be reached, by verifying against the trust the platform actually holds instead of matching a vendor name in a distinguished name, and by reporting an unverifiable certificate rather than silently refusing it.
output_contract: A PAN transport that verifies a chain instead of matching a vendor name
An unverifiable certificate reported with its fingerprint and no identity values
A measured statement on whether the runtime JVM trusts the corporate CA
An open pull request number against main

recommended_reasoning.reason: A TLS trust boundary in the device transport, where the wrong shape of fix silently weakens verification rather than failing loudly.

requirements: A certificate issued by a CA the platform trusts is accepted, whatever organisation name it carries
A certificate that fails chain verification or validity is not silently accepted
The organisation-name string match is gone; no code decides trust from a distinguished name
When verification fails, the recorded outcome names the failure class and carries the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint, so the operator can pin it through the existing pinned-fingerprint path
No distinguished name, subject, host name or address reaches a stored failure summary
If the JVM does not see the corporate CA material the image installs, that is fixed here and the fix is stated in the report
risks: Do not replace one invented control with another. If chain verification cannot be performed, say so and report it; do not fall back to a name check, a host name check, or an accept-all manager.
The fingerprint is an identifier: render and record it exactly as computed, never shortened or reformatted.

The frontend test runner needs node_modules, which a fresh worktree does not carry. If a frontend command is needed and cannot start, link or install ui2/frontend dependencies and run it rather than reporting BLOCKED with work unvalidated.
mvn test is the gate here; a green compile is not a green gate.
